jobs.title: Staff Power Systems Site Integration Engineer
jobs.description:
### **About Mainspring**

Mainspring Energy manufactures and delivers fuel-flexible, low-emissions local power solutions that rapidly add new capacity and deliver reliable, affordable, and sustainable electric power. The company began commercial shipments of its Mainspring Linear Generators in 2020 and today has hundreds of megawatts in advanced development and field operations for leading Fortune 500 companies, data centers, and utilities. Mainspring also partners with global energy leaders including AEP, NextEra Energy Resources, Schneider Electric, and more.

The core values that ground our work, guide our decisions, and connect us together:

* Pragmatic Optimism
* Excellence without Ego
* Proactive Collaboration

### **Job Overview**

Site Integration Engineers report to the Project Engineering Manager within the Project Delivery department. A key enabler of Mainspring’s mission is the ability of its team to deliver solutions based on our linear generator technology that solve customer problems in the cross-section of resiliency and clean power supply.

The project engineering team provides the technical expertise, guidance, and support to deploy linear generators into the field efficiently—building customer confidence and enabling future scalability. This role owns site-level readiness after construction is complete, ensuring that all mechanical, electrical, control, and communication systems are fully integrated, validated, and ready to transition into commissioning and operation. Generator commissioning is performed by a separate team; this role ensures the site is ready for it. Acting as the technical integration authority on site, this role bridges engineering design intent and real-world system operation.

### **Responsibilities**

This role will be responsible for:

* Interpreting technical project details, including scopes of work, sequences of operation, control narratives, and engineering drawings (site plans, P&IDs, single-line, and three-line diagrams), and serving as the controls subject matter expert in design reviews
* Verifying relay settings, meter configurations, and controller programming delivered by third-party integrators against approved settings files and design documents
* Owning site readiness on assigned projects by validating installation quality and accuracy of balance-of-plant systems such as fuel, electrical, metering, protection relays, and communications; developing punch lists and driving issues to closure when discrepancies are found
* Validating electrical and mechanical installations against drawings and specifications by witnessing and/or reviewing results of checks such as wiring and termination verification, grounding, insulation resistance and continuity testing, phase rotation, and electrical acceptance test (NETA) reports; and equipment setting and anchoring, gas piping pressure and leak tests, purging, ventilation and exhaust, and fuel regulator setup
* Configuring equipment and verifying functional readiness of site-level control and communication systems prior to energization, including troubleshooting industrial communication networks (e.g., Modbus TCP/IP, EtherNet/IP, Profibus, OPC-UA)
* Supporting integration with customer PLC/SCADA/HMI platforms (e.g., Ignition, SEL RTAC, Siemens WinCC, AVEVA Wonderware, Rockwell FactoryTalk, Schneider EcoStruxure) for system monitoring and control
* Coordinating handoff to the generator commissioning team, confirming all site-level prerequisites are complete before units are started, and keeping project stakeholders updated on readiness status and next steps
* Planning Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) and system-level validation, defining acceptance criteria for customer and utility witness testing, and confirming that as-built operation matches design intent
* Supporting Permission to Operate (PTO) by compiling documentation based on utility requirements and building an accurate submission package for the Interconnection team to issue to the utility
* Owning site QA/QC documentation and ensuring systems are fully validated and ready for turnover to operations and the customer
* Establishing repeatable processes, including ready-for-commissioning and ready-for-testing checklists, lookahead dashboards, SAT templates, equipment configuration and how-to guides, site procedures, etc
* Travelling to project sites as needed to confirm readiness and perform necessary testing

### **Job Qualifications and Experience**

* B.S. degree in Electrical, Controls, Mechatronics, or a related engineering discipline. Equivalent field experience may be substituted
* 5+ years in pre-commissioning, site commissioning, field applications, or controls engineering on power generation, battery storage, solar, microgrid, or industrial facility projects
* Experience configuring, integrating, and troubleshooting devices and platforms such as:
  + Protective relays and automation controllers: SEL (relays, RTAC), GE Multilin, Beckwith, or ABB.
  + Revenue and power quality meters: SEL-735, Schneider ION, GE kV2c, or Itron
  + PLCs: Allen-Bradley ControlLogix/CompactLogix, Siemens S7, or Schneider Modicon
  + SCADA/HMI: Ignition, Siemens WinCC, AVEVA (Wonderware), or Rockwell FactoryTalk View
* Working knowledge of industrial communication protocols (Modbus TCP/IP, EtherNet/IP, Profibus, OPC-UA, DNP3) and OT networking
* Ability to interpret single-line and three-line diagrams, P&IDs, control narratives, and sequences of operation
* Understanding of balance-of-plant systems, including fuel/gas, low- and medium-voltage electrical, metering, protection, and communications, with the ability to read construction plan sets and acceptance test reports and a working knowledge of NEC and NFPA 37/54
* Experience planning and documenting Site Acceptance Testing and supporting utility witness testing for PTO
* Familiarity with field safety practices and energization standards and procedures (e.g., NFPA 70E, lockout/tagout), including Lockout/Ta

The role provides key insight into data architecture, data modeling, and application development and engages in all aspects of the development life cycle as needed for each project to be successful. The ideal candidate will be responsible for modeling clinical data within the Databricks environment, developing and maintaining scalable data pipelines, and modernizing legacy ETL processes for cloud environments. The position will also support data quality, performance optimization, monitoring, and general Databricks computing needs for research and analytical applications.

**About WorkOS**

WorkOS builds modern developer tools and APIs that make it easy for companies to become Enterprise Ready. Our platform powers authentication, identity, authorization, and other critical infrastructure that developers need to securely scale their products to large organizations.  
  
We recently raised a $100M Series C, valuing the company at $2B, led by Meritech and Sapphire with participation from Greenoaks, Craft, Abstract, and Audacious. WorkOS powers enterprise features for many of the fastest-growing AI companies, including OpenAI, Cursor, and Perplexity, Sierra, and Plaid.  
  
As AI reshapes software, WorkOS is at the frontier of Human and Agent Authentication, Identity, and Access Control helping companies answer a new critical question: who are your agents, and what are they allowed to do? Our fast-growing customer base includes hundreds of modern software companies building the next generation of enterprise-ready products.

**About the role**
------------------

The Data team at WorkOS plays a central role on the company operations to ensure information and insights are accurate and available from any surface, whether that's a visualization tool or an agent's response, to accelerate company growth and scale. The team owns WorkOS's internal data platform end to end: ingestion, orchestration, the Snowflake warehouse, dbt transformations, governance and access controls. We also own the consumption layer: the reverse-ETL syncs that land data in Salesforce and Slack, the semantic views that agents query, the definitions that keep reporting consistent across the company, and the visualization tooling the company uses (ask us about Flashboards).

We run on an agent-first operating system: we are a lean team that moves fast, we document so agents can execute, and AI agents query the warehouse, run our runbooks, and open pull requests alongside us. We trust each other's expertise, we work out loud and in the open, and not opposed to rapid experimentation to get to the right solution for the business.

This is a high-ownership role on a lean team: you will be the DRI for the platform and its core data models, partner directly with Product Engineering, RevOps, Finance, GTM Engineering, and Security, and raise the bar on reliability, correctness, and operational rigor. The role spans the platform and what runs on it. You will own ingestion, orchestration, and access governance; the dbt models and metric definitions that depend on them; and how AI is applied across the data stack, so that trusted data is easy for both people and AI agents to discover, understand, and work with.

You don't need to have done this exact job before. The best data engineers at WorkOS are the ones who notice in a Slack thread that a number doesn't match, trace it from the dashboard through the Gold model to the connector, fix the connector, and confirm the definition with its owner before the weekly review. When a business team asks for a field in Salesforce, they don't hand it off; they build the model, write the sync, and add the test. They would rather automate the runbook than run it a third time. They enjoy collaboration with different parts of the business and can find simple, scalable solutions to ambiguous problems. If that sounds like how you work, we want to talk.

* Design, build, and scale the core dbt models (Bronze, Silver, Gold) for billing and usage, CRM, product events, and GTM funnel reporting
* Partner with Product, Finance, RevOps, and GTM to define metrics and codify them in the warehouse, and diagnose and resolve data quality and freshness issues at source, not just downstream
* Own Snowflake RBAC, dynamic masking, and PII classification for humans, agents, and service accounts, so sensitive data is protected without blocking legitimate use, and review DDL and access requests from Engineering and GTM
* Own the reverse-ETL layer and the runbooks that deliver warehouse data to Salesforce, Slack, and internal agents
* Extend the semantic views, context, and evaluations that let agents answer business questions accurately, and expand what agents can operate directly, from runbooks and ingestion to pull requests
* Build and advance the CI/CD review gates in the data-platform monorepo, including the automated review that agent-authored pull requests pass through
* Own the infrastructure the data platform runs on: the compute, deployments, secrets and access patterns, and environments behind ingestion and orchestration, with attention to availability and failure modes, in partnership with our infrastructure engineers

Example problems you might work on, possible paths rather than a fixed roadmap:

* Standardizing how Postgres and SaaS sources are ingested, and consolidating end-to-end pipeline deployment and orchestration in Prefect
* Managing Snowflake RBAC, resource management, and masking policies as code with Terraform
* Using query history to improve analytics tables and semantic views, and to keep agent answers accurate and consistent as data grows and metrics shift
* Automating masking coverage as new data sources arrive, so adding a new table no longer needs a human in the loop

* Pseudonymizing product data in the ingestion path, alongside compliance and data-deletion policies
* Extending transcript aggregation across sources, including PII detection before transcripts enter the warehouse

new_jobs.description:
**About Anthropic**
-------------------

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About the role**
------------------

Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. Security at that scale runs on data, and you'll be the engineer who owns it and the systems that produce it: component-level hardware inventory and chain of custody, fed by software that runs at our sites and on hosts, and continuous control monitoring, with the posture calculations that decide what each site is cleared to run.

You set the architecture, agree schemas and interfaces with the teams, operators and vendors that own the sources, build the pipelines, stores and tools, and run what you ship. The goal is security that runs itself: custody, access and evidence verified continuously from records, with tools and AI agents doing the reviews. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well.

You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's compute and data center operations teams, and directly with data center operators, hardware vendors and logistics providers. The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure.

**Key responsibilities**
------------------------

* **Hardware inventory and chain of custody:** own the component-level record of what hardware exists, where it is and who has handled it: the data model, the pipelines that join inventory and custody events from many source systems, change history on every record, and the tamper-evident stores behind it

new_jobs.title: Data Engineer, Ingestion Platform
new_jobs.description:
**Location**
------------

Remote

**Employment Type**
-------------------

Full time

**Location Type**
-----------------

Remote

**Department**
--------------

Product and Data

**Compensation**
----------------

* $155K – $165K • Offers Equity

  

Alt is unlocking the value of alternative assets, starting with the $5 B trading-card market. We let collectors buy, sell, vault, and finance their cards in one place and we are backed by leaders at Stripe, Coinbase, Seven Seven Six, and pro athletes like Tom Brady and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Our next frontier is real-time pricing at scale—the Alt Value that powers every trade, loan, and product on the platform.

**The Role**
------------

Alt Value is our moat. It is only as good as the data underneath it — and that data lives on dozens of external marketplaces and auction houses that have no interest in making it easy for us to get.

That's this job. You own the pipelines that scrape, normalize, and land every transaction and listing that feeds our pricing model. When a comparable sale closes on eBay or at a major auction house, how fast it shows up in Alt Value, and whether it shows up correctly, is your call and your consequence. Pricing decisions, cash advance terms, market analytics, and every dashboard in the company sit downstream of you.

**The metric you own: Data Coverage.** Supporting KPIs are pipeline latency, uptime, and source coverage.

**What You'll Own:**
--------------------

* **The ingestion layer.** Design, optimize, and own the pipelines that scrape, process, and ingest transaction and listing data from major auction houses and marketplaces. Scraper to orchestrator to warehouse, end to end.
* **Build for reuse first.** Most of the ingestion stack — auth handling, retries, session and proxy management, monitoring — should generalize across sources. Go deep and custom only where a specific source's structure actually requires it.
* **Knowing before we do.** Build the monitoring and alerting that tracks latency, uptime, and coverage across every source. A source going quiet should page you, not surprise a pricer three days later.
* **Making it cheaper and steadier.** Modernize storage and processing, cut manual intervention out of the loop, and optimize for cost, performance, and reliability.
* **The consumers.** Partner with pricing, ML, product, and analytics to deliver data clean and standardized enough that nobody downstream is writing defensive code around your output.

**How You'll Use AI Here:**
---------------------------

We don't want to hear that you use Claude every day. Everyone does. We want to know what you've built with it. Concretely, in this role:

* Point an agent at a **site that just changed its markup** and have it propose the parser fix, run it against a fixture set, and open the PR
* Build a **triage loop over the orchestrator** — cross-reference a failed DAG against logs and warehouse state, diagnose the cause, and hand you a ranked list instead of a wall of red
* Use **LLM extraction for the long tail** of low-volume sources where a bespoke scraper will never pay for itself
* Put an **MCP server over the warehouse** so a coverage question is a sentence, not another one-off query
* Use **Claude Code or Cursor** as the default way you work through a migration or a backfill, not as autocomplete

If you've built agents, written skills or MCP servers, wired up connectors, or shipped internal tooling your team actually depends on — lead with that.

**What You Bring:**
-------------------

* 3-4 years in data engineering or a closely adjacent seat.
* Modern web scraping at scale — Playwright or comparable, plus the ability to impersonate a real browser at the network layer (TLS/request fingerprinting) when a plain HTTP client gets flagged. Selenium alone doesn't cut it anymore.
* Strong Python, 3+ years hands-on. Solid SQL for analysis and transformation.
* A pipeline you owned end to end in the past two years. Not a pipeline you contributed to. One that was yours when it broke.
* Judgment on when to generalize and when to go bespoke — you don't rebuild the same infrastructure per source, and you don't force a one-size-fits-all approach onto a source that needs custom handling.
* Orchestration in your hands, not your resume. Airflow, Dagster, or a comparable DAG system — you've built on it, been paged for it, and cleaned up after it.
* Cloud development experience (AWS, GCP).
* LLM-based extraction and processing at scale (e.g. LLM-as-a-Judge, Agent loops), not just UI-based Q&A and simple Skill building.
* Startup experience. You understand the pace, and you've worked somewhere the roadmap changed under you.
* A pragmatic bias. Value delivered incrementally over the perfect rebuild.

**Bonus:** large-scale dataframe processing (Pandas, Polars, PySpark). You collect, or you have opinions about the collectibles market.

**How We'll Interview You:**
----------------------------

We'll be specific so you can prepare. *Before any of it: download the app, put a card up, make a bid, or put a card up for sell. Every round assumes you've used the product, and we expect your point of view to sharpen as you go.*

**1. Recruiter screen - 30 minutes** Come ready to talk about the metric you own today, why Alt specifically, and how you're actually using AI. We'll answer your questions and align on comp.

**2. Hiring manager with Dae, Head of Data — 30 minutes.** Be ready to go deep on one pipeline you owned end to end: the systems design, what you owned versus the team, where it broke, and what came out the other side.

**3. Coding screen — 45 minutes.** A working session on a data problem close to what this role actually does.

**4. Systems design — 60 minutes.** Design an ingestion system under real constraints. We'll push back on at least one of your choices on purpose — how you take that matters as much as the design.

**5. Cross-functional — 60 Mins** How you work with the people downstream of your data.

**6.

As a Backend / Data Engineer on the Coverage Intelligence team, you build the data foundation and services that turn coverage intelligence into a dependable production capability inside the Digital Exchange, powered by DeX ai. You own how data moves through the system, from ingestion through to the products that rely on it, and you make sure it is accurate, traceable and secure. You work closely with AI engineers and domain specialists, and help shape the team’s data and platform architecture as it grows.

  

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

  

* Design, build and operate the pipelines and data stores behind coverage intelligence.
* Build the services and data contracts that deliver coverage insights to other teams and products.
* Ensure every result can be traced back to its source, with strong data quality and lineage.
* Build the data infrastructure that lets the team measure accuracy and improve it with every release.
* Own the reliability, performance and cost of the team’s production services.
* Uphold security and privacy standards for sensitive policy and customer data.
* Partner with engineers and specialists across teams to integrate coverage data into the wider platform.
* Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

**YOUR LOCATION**  
This is a fully remote role, with the exception of onboarding and optional in-office events.

  

**SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS**

  

* 5+ years’ experience in backend or data engineering, building and operating production services and pipelines.
* Strong Python and SQL.
* Experience with MongoDB and relational databases (PostgreSQL or similar).
* Experience designing APIs and data contracts consumed by other teams.
* Experience with workflow orchestration (e.g., Prefect or Airflow) and batch and event-driven processing.
* Hands-on AWS experience, including containers, infrastructure as code and observability tooling.
* Experience modeling versioned, effective-dated reference data.
* Working knowledge of CI/CD pipelines.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Works autonomously with minimal direction, sets a clear path through ambiguity, and holds a high bar for quality.
* Thrives on the energy of a start up: comfortable with pace, changing priorities, and building the function while running it.
* Experience supporting machine learning or LLM systems in production, such as data pipelines, evaluation data or model serving (strongly preferred).
* Experience with search stores such as OpenSearch (preferred).
* Experience supporting LLM observability or evaluation tooling (preferred).
* Insurance or insurtech experience, including familiarity with insurance concepts and insurance-specific canonical data models (preferred).

**Physical Requirements**

* Must be able to sit/stand/walk for prolonged periods of time (up to 8 hours per day), at a desk working on a computer.
* Must be able to use standard office equipment for extended periods of time, including but not limited to, a mouse, keyboard, phone and video conferencing.
* Must be able to travel to the Bold Penguin office in Dublin, Ohio for New Hire Onboarding & Orientation (2 days, 2 nights); travel costs are covered by Bold Penguin.
* Must be able to travel occasionally (up to 10%) for corporate events and team planning sessions.

Bold Penguin is the premier digital broker for commercial insurance. Their technology expands top-of-funnel demand and increases yield for enterprise partners. Through digital distribution, wholesale capabilities, and AI-driven insights, they transform the lifecycle of both simple and complex risks, from prospecting to placement.

**Benefits**

  

We offer competitive compensation and progressive benefits that include:

* Medical, Dental, and Vision
* Flexible PTO Policy
* 401(k) with a company match
* Employee Assistance Program
* Parental Leave
* Disability and Life Benefits

**Stay connected to the Glacier.** We have great SLACK channels for work and play. We also like to video conference and hold all-hands "Waddles" regularly.

**Penguin bling.** Like swag themed after a certain Antarctic bird? Just. You. Wait.

Bold Penguin believes in inclusion. That’s why we’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer that considers all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. To learn more about our results-focused culture and employee-focused perks, read more on our **careers page**.

**About Spoiler Alert**
-----------------------

Spoiler Alert is a CPG and retail tech company on a mission to expand consumer access to affordable, everyday essentials by unlocking the value in surplus inventory. We've powered the sale of over $6 billion of inventory from leading CPG brands like Unilever, Kraft Heinz, and Mondelez into hundreds of value channel retailers and wholesalers - recovering value for brands, reducing waste, and creating savings for consumers. We're building the marketplace infrastructure to transform CPG surplus into opportunity for retailers to meet consumer demand at scale, and infusing AI-native products into a segment of the CPG supply chain that is ripe for improvement.

**Role**
--------

We're hiring a **Senior Data Engineer** to build and own the data infrastructure that powers Spoiler Alert's next chapter. Our platform generates unique data across every supplier and buyer transaction, and how well we move, model, and make that data accessible determines our company’s ability to produce results for our industry. Decision intelligence, AI-powered pricing recommendations, demand matching, customer-facing analytics will all run on the foundation this role helps build.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role for someone who takes ownership of systems end-to-end and sets the bar for the team around them. You'll work at the intersection of data, product, and platform engineering, partnering closely with Data and Product teams to make our data reliable, accessible, and useful for internal decisions and for our customers. You'll bring strong opinions about what good data infrastructure looks like, use AI tools appropriately as a genuine part of how you work, and help establish what that looks like for the team.

This role partners closely with the Data and Product teams.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

**Build & own the data platform**

* Architect, build, and maintain the infrastructure that moves and transforms Spoiler Alert's marketplace data reliably and at scale, effectively incorporating AI coding tools to build with quality and velocity

* Design and enforce data quality standards across the stack, defining what trusted data means at Spoiler Alert and developing the monitoring and testing that upholds it
* Make intentional architectural decisions with the appropriate level of abstraction, documenting decisions and tradeoffs so the team can build confidently on your work, including data infrastructure for effective product applications of AI/ML

**Raise the bar for engineering quality**

* Contribute exemplary code in pipeline logic, SQL, and data modeling that other engineers learn from and build on
* Share meaningful code reviews that evolve our team's patterns and practices
* Debug and resolve data issues quickly, and drive root cause work that prevents them from recurring
* Contribute to shared support responsibilities and help build a culture of reliability across the data platform

**Lead technically across the team**

* Take end-to-end accountability for data systems and roadmap themes, owning projects through from design to production to iteration, communicating tradeoffs and risks along the way
* Partner with Product, Data, and Engineering teammates to ensure our pipelines, models, and tooling support reliable internal and external decision making using our data
* Identify opportunities where better data infrastructure creates leverage for Product, Data, Engineering, and Operations teams, and advocate for those investments with clarity
* Contribute meaningfully to architecture conversations and Engineering reflection, shaping technical decisions with your expertise

**Qualifications**
------------------

* 5–8+ years of data engineering experience, ideally at a B2B SaaS, marketplace, or data products company
* Deep hands-on expertise across the modern data stack, including pipeline tooling (we use Estuary), workflow orchestration (we use Astronomer Airflow), transformations (we use dbt), and BI tools with semantic layers (we use Holistics)
* Strong SQL and data modeling foundations for clean, well-structured models that others can build on and maintain
* Experience owning data quality end-to-end, including testing and observability frameworks infrastructure and tools with a genuine bias for reliability
* AI-native chops: you productively integrate AI into your development workflows to build with curiosity and strong opinions loosely held
* Proven ability to take accountability for systems and themes, not just individual tasks or projects. You see the work through and communicate clearly along the way.
* Ability to collaborate cross functionally with data analysts, product engineers, and non-technical stakeholders, bringing clarity to ambiguity
* Experience differentiators: marketplace or transaction-platform data, applied AI/ML pipeline work, customer-facing analytics products, food and beverage or CPG domain knowledge, experience integrating LLM tooling into data workflows

At EAB, our mission is to make education smarter and our communities stronger. We work with more than 2,800 institutions to drive transformative change through data-driven insights and best-in-class capabilities. From kindergarten to college to career, EAB partners with leaders and practitioners to accelerate progress and drive results across enrollment, student success, institutional strategy, data analytics, and advancement. We work with each partner differently, tailoring our portfolio of research, technology, and marketing and enrollment solutions to meet the unique needs of every leadership team, as well as the students and employees they serve.

At EAB, we serve not only our partner institutions but each other—that's why we are always working to make sure our employees love their jobs and are invested in their communities. See how we've been recognized for this dedication to our employees by checking out our recent awards.

For more information, visit our Careers page.

Join Workiva's GRC (Governance, Risk & Compliance) Enablement team to build the transactional data foundations that power our product teams. As a Staff Data Engineer, you'll own Postgres schema design, transactional data models, and the extraction layer that feeds our OLAP systems. You'll work alongside an OLAP specialist on this team (same manager) to jointly own GRC data outcomes end to end, transactional models through BI and history marts, and you'll partner closely with the platform data team on shared infrastructure and tooling. Your job is to make sure GRC product teams have data systems that are reliable, well-modeled, and easy to build against, and to raise the data fluency of engineers across the org.

  

This is a heavily hands-on role. You'll design schemas, define extraction and CDC patterns, and mentor engineers who need to write better queries and reason about relational data at scale. Together with the OLAP specialist on this team, you'll own the full data lifecycle for GRC: transactional models, BI marts, and history marts.

  

**What you'll do**
------------------

*Transactional database design & operations*

* Design, review, and evolve Postgres schemas for GRC product services, balancing normalization, query performance, and application ergonomics.
* Set standards for indexing, constraints, partitioning, and connection pooling; identify and resolve performance bottlenecks in production.
* Own migration strategy and tooling (schema changes, backfills, zero-downtime deploys) across services.

*OLTP-to-OLAP extraction (owned) / transformation (shared boundary with OLAP)*

* Own change-data-capture and extraction: what leaves Postgres, in what shape, on what cadence, and how upstream schema changes are communicated before they break downstream models.
* Define the data contract at the landing zone with the OLAP specialist so extraction output is stable and well-documented; you own upstream reliability, they own what happens after landing.
* Where dbt/ETL logic sits closer to source-of-truth semantics (e.g., early-stage transaction or history-mart models), collaborate with the OLAP specialist to determine ownership on a per-project basis, documented explicitly rather than left implicit.

*Data modeling & query performance*

* Establish relational modeling patterns and review standards so engineers build consistent, maintainable schemas.
* Optimize SQL for transactional workloads (query plans, indexing strategy, lock contention, multi-join performance at scale).
* Define data contracts between services so schema changes don't silently break consumers, including downstream OLAP consumers.

*Reliability, security & compliance*

* Implement data integrity checks, replication/failover practices, and monitoring for transactional data health and extraction pipelines.
* Work within regulated release pipelines using GitOps/CI/CD; manage schema and pipeline promotions through dev/test/prod with gated approvals.
* Apply RBAC, audit logging, and encryption standards aligned with Workiva's information-protection policies, at the OLTP layer and extraction layer specifically.

*Technical leadership & enablement*

* Establish schema design patterns, SQL coding standards, and documentation so engineers can confidently build against Postgres without escalating every decision.
* Mentor engineers on relational modeling, query optimization, and transactional system fundamentals; lead incident resolution and root-cause analysis for production data issues, including extraction failures.
* Partner with the OLAP specialist to define and document where responsibility splits, and revisit that boundary as the platform matures.
Partner with the platform data team on infrastructure decisions (warehouse provisioning, streaming infra, CI/CD tooling) while retaining ownership of GRC-specific schema design, modeling standards, and data quality outcomes; this team owns the "what and how" of GRC data models, platform data team owns the "on what infrastructure."  

  
  

**What you'll need**
--------------------

*Minimum qualifications*

* 5+ years in data engineering or backend engineering with hands-on ownership of production Postgres (or comparable relational OLTP) systems.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.  

  

*Preferred qualifications*

* Proven experience owning schema design and migrations for production Postgres services at scale.

**CANDIDATES MUST BE LOCATED IN THE UNITED STATES OR CANADA**

**About SafelyYou**

SafelyYou’s passionate mission is to empower safer, more person-centered care across senior living through world-leading AI, industry-changing hardware, and remote expert clinicians, significantly improving outcomes for residents while increasing peace of mind for families and reducing costs for communities.  
  
Originating in 2015 as the doctoral research of CEO George Netscher—and inspired by his own family's experience with Alzheimer's disease—SafelyYou was spun out of UC Berkeley’s Artificial Intelligence Research Lab, one of the top five AI research groups in the world. And today, our company is solving critical challenges in senior living, from resident falls and ER visits to staffing concerns, length of stay, and NOI. All helping ensure that communities can focus on improved care for residents while still reaching their financial goals.  
  
SafelyYou is one of five most innovative fall technologies referenced in the Senate Falls Report (2019), a winner of the McKnight’s Tech Partner of the Year, and has been named to Fortune’s Impact 20 list, which recognizes companies making people’s lives better through innovation.

**Your Role at SafelyYou**  
  
As a Data Integration Engineer at SafelyYou, you will be the subject matter expert behind how our internal systems communicate with the outside world. You will design, build, and operate robust integration pipelines that transform data between our internal event-based architecture and the diverse formats required by our third-party API partners. You will play a critical role in scaling our external data exchange capabilities, handling complex payload mappings, and ensuring that our systems gracefully manage failure modes at scale.

You will work closely with R&D architects, other data engineers, backend developers, and cross-functional teams to define and implement integration patterns for webhooks, external REST APIs, and partner platforms. Additionally, you will own technical communications for integrations, managing Go-Live data backfills and writing clear API specifications for customer-facing documents.

This is a fully remote role. You are expected to work with minimal guidance, act as a subject matter expert for integration patterns, and proactively identify opportunities for architectural improvement.  
  
**Key Responsibilities:**

* Design, build, and operate robust integration pipelines to ingest data from and push data to third-party APIs, webhooks, and custom endpoints.
* Transform, normalize, and map data payloads between SafelyYou’s internal schema and external partner specifications (e.g., JSON/XML schemas, third-party platforms).
* Performing validation on data received from third-parties, segregating data that fails validation, and automating processes with third-parties to resolve anomalies.
* Manage and execute complex data backfills and Go-Live integration pipelines for new customer rollouts.
* Write and maintain clear, high-quality technical documentation and API specifications for both internal engineering teams and external partners.
* Triage, troubleshoot, and gracefully handle integration failure modes, rate limits, and edge cases at scale, building resilient retry mechanisms.
* Scale our ability to support 3rd party integrations by building systems and tooling to allow non-engineer users to configure, monitor, and perform backfills for third-party integrations.
* Ensure data quality, consistency, and reliability by developing automated tests and validating payload outputs with ongoing pipeline monitoring.
* Work in an Agile environment to plan, track, and improve the delivery of new integration features and products.
* Collaborate with customer support, operations, and product teams to provide technical support and participate in on-call rotation as needed.

**Requirements:**

* 5+ years of professional experience in software, backend, or data engineering, preferably in a startup environment.
* Deep hands-on experience building, consuming, and operating integrations with REST APIs, webhooks, and third-party platforms.
* Strong programming proficiency in Python and SQL for building reliable data transformation and integration pipelines.
* Proven track record of handling complex data transformations, schema mapping, and payload normalization across disparate systems.
* Experience encountering and solving API failure modes and operational challenges at scale (e.g., implementing exponential backoff, dead-letter queues, idempotency). Has seen where things fail and can recommend solutions to maintain a stable platform.
* Strong verbal and written communication skills, with specific experience writing technical documentation, ADRs, or API specs.
* Proactive about anticipating and addressing data ingestion issues before they impact the business.
* Prioritize quality over speed. When it is done, it is really done.

**The Ideal Candidate:**

* Proficiency with modern data stack tools, such as dbt and PySpark.
* Familiarity with workflow orchestration concepts and tools, such as Airflow.
* Exposure to Terraform and Cloud Infrastructure, such as AWS (Athena, RDS, EKS).
* Experience with electronic health records (EHR) and associated data privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA) is a strong plus.
* Experience with HL7 data feeds and the FHIR API specification is a huge plus.
* Experience with remote work and distributed, async-first engineering teams.

**Why Join Us? You Can Make a Difference!**

new_jobs.description:
Big Data Engineer is a remote engineering review track for evaluating production code, debugging traces, and developer-facing AI outputs against real-world correctness standards. Reviewers reproduce failures, write the unit test the model should have written, and explain the fix so the modeling team can target the gap.

**Why this role matters**
-------------------------

Engineering model quality lives or dies on whether the generated code actually compiles, passes tests, and handles edge cases. AuraOne pairs experienced engineers with the modeling team to grade outputs the way a code reviewer would.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Run and reproduce candidate code outputs in a sandboxed environment for Big Data Engineer assignments.
* Grade data engineering solutions for correctness, style, and edge-case handling.
* Write minimal failing tests that demonstrate the bug a model output missed.
* Compare paired solutions and rank them with a written rationale tied to the rubric.
* Tag failure modes (compile error, runtime crash, off-by-one, security issue) with severity scores.
* Document recurring code-generation failures so the modeling team can target them.
* Calibrate against gold-standard reviews to keep inter-rater agreement above target.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Strong day-job engineering experience — you can read, run, and debug unfamiliar code for Big Data Engineer work.
* Comfort writing concise unit tests that capture a single failure mode.
* Familiarity with a testing framework. pytest, Jest, or JUnit. Go test, RSpec, or whatever you use.
* Clear written reasoning — your review note has to convince another senior engineer.
* Reliable async availability for at least 10 hours per week.
* Prior code-review or technical-interview-grading experience is a plus.

**Example tasks**
-----------------

* Reproduce a generated engineering solution to a coding task, run the test suite, and grade it.
* Write the smallest failing test that demonstrates a model's edge-case bug.
* Compare two paired solutions and rank them with a written rationale tied to the rubric.
* Triage a security issue surfaced by a model and document the patch the model should have produced.

**Nice to have**
----------------

* Open-source contributions or a public portfolio that demonstrates production-quality code.
* Experience with the target language's standard tooling, linters, and idiomatic style guides.
* Familiarity with security-review checklists (OWASP, CWE) and AppSec patterns.

**Skills**
----------

* Code review
* Debugging
* Unit testing
* Software engineering judgment
* Data engineering

**Work model**
--------------

Remote — US-eligible. Remote · Independent specialist contractor. Employment type: CONTRACTOR. Applicants must be authorized to work from US.

**Compensation**
----------------

Hourly rate confirmed after the interview process.

Apply through AuraOne's specialist intake for role-specific routing and review. Final project scope, schedule, and contractor terms are confirmed before placement.

new_jobs.description:
### **This is a Remote Position. US based role only. No HB-1 Visa Support** **OUR VISION**

Equs is a company building privacy-first AI, identity, and trust infrastructure for the agentic era. The digital world was built around platforms, not people. AI is rewriting what software can do, and we have a narrow window to make sure that future puts the individual at the center rather than further behind. We start from one conviction: your digital identity should belong to you, travel with you, and give you real agency in how you show up online. You set the rules, you hold the keys, and you benefit from your own data.  
  
We are building toward that future across every layer it requires: the infrastructure that makes it possible, the standards that make it interoperable, and the experiences that bring it to life for the people who use it. We are early, and we are clear about what is built today and what is still ahead. The people who use what we build keep control of their own data, and we hold ourselves to that standard in everything we make.

### **WHAT YOU WILL DO**

We’re taking the EQUS Developer Toolkit to organizations of all kinds, from banks and other regulated institutions to employers, education providers, public bodies and digital platforms, and every one of them needs someone technical on our side to get them live. This is our first dedicated integration hire and a hands-on, customer-facing role. You’ll be the technical lead for each customer from the first architecture call to the first credential in production: designing the solution, connecting their identity and back-end systems, and guiding them through security review. You’ll bring what you learn back into the product and the docs, and help shape how integration works as the team grows. You may be required to work on other EQUS products over time. Your day-to-day includes, but is not limited to:

* Designing each customer’s solution, turning use cases such as KYC status, employee or student IDs, qualifications, age checks, membership and AI-agent payment mandates into a Developer Toolkit design (issuance and presentation flows, wallet model and build method) that the customer’s architects can sign off
* Running technical onboarding, provisioning sandbox and production tenants, issuing client credentials, setting up Issuers, Verifiers and credential schemas with the customer, and enabling and tracking on-request features such as the Web Wallet, AP2 agent flows and quota increases
* Connecting customer identity systems, guiding IAM teams through Bring Your Own IdP (OpenID Connect), Authorization Server registration and OAuth client-credentials setup in both directions
* Getting back-end integrations live, specifying and reviewing each customer’s Attribute Provider endpoint and helping their engineers debug using request IDs, error codes and rate-limit headers
* Supporting front-end teams as they embed our UI within strict security policies and allowed-origin rules, apply their branding, and enable the browser Digital Credentials API where devices support it
* Leading EU Digital Identity Wallet readiness, from moving Verifiers to X.509 and securing registration certificates from national Registrars to configuring trusted roots
* Owning the technical side of security and procurement, answering due-diligence questionnaires and joining security reviews using our data-handling, encryption, DPA and TOMs documentation
* Supporting business development in technical sales conversations, helping prospective customers understand what an integration involves and helping us close our first deals
* Acting as the customer’s voice to product, logging and prioritizing the gaps that block deals and working with our engineering team and partners on fixes
* Making every integration faster than the last, writing quickstarts, help-center articles, sample code and a reusable customer integration pack with sector variants, including a flow decision tree, security answers and a go-live checklist

### **WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO SUCCEED**

You combine deep technical skill with real empathy for customers, and you’re as comfortable with a bank’s IAM team as with a startup’s two developers. You’re fluent in OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect and can work out why a token is rejected, you can read an OpenAPI spec and write enough back-end code to build sample integrations, and you understand PKI well enough to untangle a certificate chain. You write clearly, whether it’s an integration design, a security answer or public documentation. You are comfortable with ambiguity, because parts of our product are still being built and you’ll design around the roadmap. You are self-directed in a remote setting, managing your own time and keeping several customer integrations moving at once.

### **YOUR EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

This role calls for 4 or more years in a customer-facing technical role such as solutions engineer, integration engineer or technical consultant for an API or identity product. You’ve personally taken enterprise customers from pilot to production, ideally in regulated or security-conscious sectors such as banking, insurance, government, healthcare or education, including security reviews and vendor due diligence. You bring hands-on experience with REST APIs and at least one back-end language (TypeScript/Node, Java/Kotlin or Python), and a working understanding of X.509 certificates, trust anchors and key management. Experience with verifiable credentials and digital identity standards (OID4VCI, OID4VP, SD-JWT VC, ISO 18013-5 mdoc), eIDAS 2.0 and the EU Digital Identity Wallet ecosystem, enterprise identity providers such as Microsoft Entra, Okta or Ping, and payments, open banking or agentic-payment protocols like AP2 are all a plus.

GitHub is changing the way the world builds secure software and we want you to help change the way we secure GitHub. WorkOS builds modern developer tools and APIs that make it easy for companies to become Enterprise Ready. Our platform powers authentication, identity, authorization, and other critical infrastructure that developers need to securely scale their products to large organizations.  
  
We recently raised a $100M Series C, valuing the company at $2B, led by Meritech and Sapphire with participation from Greenoaks, Craft, Abstract, and Audacious. WorkOS powers enterprise features for many of the fastest-growing AI companies, including OpenAI, Cursor, and Perplexity, Sierra, and Plaid.  
  
As AI reshapes software, WorkOS is at the frontier of Human and Agent Authentication, Identity, and Access Control helping companies answer a new critical question: who are your agents, and what are they allowed to do? Our fast-growing customer base includes hundreds of modern software companies building the next generation of enterprise-ready products.

**About the role**
------------------

The Data team at WorkOS plays a central role on the company operations to ensure information and insights are accurate and available from any surface, whether that's a visualization tool or an agent's response, to accelerate company growth and scale. The team owns WorkOS's internal data platform end to end: ingestion, orchestration, the Snowflake warehouse, dbt transformations, governance and access controls. We also own the consumption layer: the reverse-ETL syncs that land data in Salesforce and Slack, the semantic views that agents query, the definitions that keep reporting consistent across the company, and the visualization tooling the company uses (ask us about Flashboards).

We run on an agent-first operating system: we are a lean team that moves fast, we document so agents can execute, and AI agents query the warehouse, run our runbooks, and open pull requests alongside us. We trust each other's expertise, we work out loud and in the open, and not opposed to rapid experimentation to get to the right solution for the business.

We're hiring a Data Engineer to own and evolve the systems that move, transform, protect, and serve data across our internal warehouse. This is a high-ownership role on a lean team: you will be the DRI for the platform and its core data models, partner directly with Product Engineering, RevOps, Finance, GTM Engineering, and Security, and raise the bar on reliability, correctness, and operational rigor. The role spans the platform and what runs on it. You will own ingestion, orchestration, and access governance; the dbt models and metric definitions that depend on them; and how AI is applied across the data stack, so that trusted data is easy for both people and AI agents to discover, understand, and work with.

You don't need to have done this exact job before. When a business team asks for a field in Salesforce, they don't hand it off; they build the model, write the sync, and add the test. They would rather automate the runbook than run it a third time. They enjoy collaboration with different parts of the business and can find simple, scalable solutions to ambiguous problems. If that sounds like how you work, we want to talk.

* Extend the semantic views, context, and evaluations that let agents answer business questions accurately, and expand what agents can operate directly, from runbooks and ingestion to pull requests
